english: don’t talk with your mouth full

terms.comment: A plain description: we have found no set phrase for this in the authors we searched (Plautus, Terence, Cicero, Horace, Martial, Juvenal, Petronius, Pliny’s letters, Seneca) or in Traupman, Morgan–Owens, or Levi–Bini. Mandere is the classical verb for chewing (Cic. N. D. 2.122). For “eat with your mouth closed”, Ōre clausō mande; Gellius’s dinner-table lecture ends when it is time “to eat and to be quiet”.

phrases.latin: tempusque esse coeperat edendī et tacendī
phrases.english: and it was time to eat and stop talking
